text: Multiple signals that are divided in frequency because they use different frequency subchannels, and they are orthogonal meaning that they do not overlap too much. That's the key idea of OFDM. And it allows it's very efficient in general as a technique of a physical layer because it allows you to send multiple signals at the same time. So you can increase the data rate at which you can transmit. With respect to when you transmit only one signal at a time. So it's like having the possibility to have multiple people, many people that transmit say something at the same time in parallel, and the receiver is able to actually capture each transmission at the same time. So it's like if I speak Italian and there is another person for example that speaks English next to me. If you are a receiver listening and you know well Italian and English, if you are actually able to do that but there are people who are able to do that, you can actually understand both of them at the same time. So you get in parallel what the person speaking Italian is.
